title: Institutional money drives price action patterns
claim: Price action patterns are repeatable because 90% of market volume is institutional trading with proven profitable systems; reading bar structure reveals institutional buying/selling behavior
support: Author argues institutional dominance creates predictable patterns; individuals cannot move market but can follow institutional intent
mechanism: Large volume by institutions establishes price levels; individuals observing bar patterns can infer institutional conviction direction

title: Trend reversals require prior trend line break
claim: A major reversal trade should only be entered after a clear break of the prior trend line, not on the first reversal bar

source.section: Example of How to Trade a Reversal

support: Example shows trader waiting for bull trend line to break before considering reversal short entry
mechanism: Trend line break signals end of institutional buying support at that level
assumptions: Market does not immediately retrace above line

title: Signal bar strength predicts reversal follow-through
claim: Strength of the reversal signal bar (size, structure, close relative to open) correlates with probability of sustained move in reversal direction

source.section: Signs of Strength in a Reversal

support: Strong reversal bars have large bodies, close in direction of reversal, often with tails opposite direction showing rejection
mechanism: Strong signal bar indicates institutional commitment to reversal direction
assumptions: Tail indicates tested and rejected prior direction

title: Climactic bar signals reversal exhaustion
claim: A bar that opens near one extreme and closes near the opposite, with body 2x larger than prior bars, often marks the final climax before reversal
support: Large range bar with extreme close indicates final capitulation of weak longs or shorts; next bar often reverses sharply
mechanism: Weak traders exit desperately at market; once all weak exits exhausted, institutions take other side; vacuum effect
assumptions: Bar is at end of sustained trend
No institutional support remains in prior trend direction
Opposite direction institutions ready to enter

title: Vacuum effect creates explosive reversals
claim: When strong institutional bears believe reversal likely but price still rising, they wait for better short entry; absence of selling pressure accelerates upward move until bears enter; sudden institutional selling then reverses market sharply
support: Author explains how momentum programs see buy pressure unopposed and accelerate; then when bears enter, all participants reverse
mechanism: Game-theoretic; rational players delay entry/exit expecting better prices; optimal entry point becomes inflection where many actors simultaneously reverse
assumptions: Trend channel or resistance level known
All strong players aware of similar thresholds

title: Reversal bar count relates to reversal magnitude
claim: Number of bars from start of trend to reversal bar correlates with magnitude of reversal move; longer trends produce larger reversals
support: Author illustrates 30-bar trend followed by 500+ pip reversal vs 5-bar trend with 50 pip reversal
mechanism: Longer trends accumulate more weak positions; when reversal triggers, more players caught wrong side

title: Wedge pattern compression predicts reversal
claim: Wedge pattern (decreasing range bars, trend line slopes inward) predicts reversal; breakout from wedge produces strong move in breakout direction
support: Examples show 10-15 bar wedges forming then breaking with large reversal moves
mechanism: Wedge formation represents confusion/equilibrium between buyers and sellers; breakout represents resolution; momentum follows breakout
assumptions: Trend line slopes match pattern rules

title: Double-top pattern filters reversal entries
claim: Double top (two price peaks near same level) followed by pullback predicts downtrend; pullback depth determines reversal strength
support: Author shows multiple examples: shallow pullback = strong downtrend, deep pullback = weak reversal or bounce
mechanism: Double top shows institutional resistance twice; pullback proves commitment to sell; shallow pullback shows strong supply above
assumptions: Pullback does not exceed first top

title: Failed breakout predicts reversal move
claim: Bar that closes above swing high but next 1-3 bars reverse back below the swing high predicts continuation selling at 60-70% success rate
support: Examples show failed breakouts triggering short entries with 60-70% success to recent swing low
mechanism: Failed breakout shows breakout buyers exhausted; weak commitment; reversal sellers enter aggressively

title: Opening hour volatility and reversal frequency vary by market time
claim: Certain hours (9:30-10:30 ET, 12-13 ET, 15-16 ET) produce more strong trend bars and reversals; other hours are choppy or range-bound
support: Author documents opening hour high volatility, midday chop, end-of-day reversal tendency
mechanism: Institutional entry/exit windows create volume surges; market participants adjust activity by hour
assumptions: Pattern holds in normal market conditions

title: Always-in discipline captures full trend move
claim: Trader should remain long on all bull bars and short on all bear bars when trend is active; exit only on stop loss or trend line break; re-entries without closing complete position captures larger moves than profit-taking exits
support: Author argues profit-taking at 1R misses opportunities for 5-10R moves; always-in mode allows riding trends fully
mechanism: Trend-following; each pullback re-entry increases position exposure to full trend
assumptions: Stop placement is objective (trend line break)

title: Scalp and daily trade profitability differs by entry timing
claim: Scalp entries (1-2 bar trades at reversal) average smaller profit per trade but higher frequency; daily entries (hold overnight) have lower win rate but larger avg profit when right
support: Author compares profit distributions: scalping produces frequent small wins, daily entries produce low-frequency large wins
mechanism: Scalp trades have lower friction (smaller P&L swings); overnight risk amplifies both win and loss magnitude
assumptions: Same entry logic applied to both timeframes
Account size sufficient for overnight gap risk

title: Fixed-risk position sizing outperforms fixed-share sizing
claim: Position size proportional to 1/stop_distance (shares = max_risk_dollar / stop_distance_ticks) maintains consistent risk across volatile and calm markets; produces more stable equity curve than fixed share sizing
support: Author advocates fixed-risk as best practice; prevents over-leverage in volatile regimes and under-deployment in calm periods
mechanism: Risk management; consistent loss magnitude leads to more predictable drawdowns
assumptions: Max risk per trade set prudently (1-2% of account)

title: Countertrend reversals beat trend-following for short-term edge
claim: Reversal trades (countertrend, small bars after climax) produce 2-3% better Sharpe than trend-following entries; requires discipline to sell strength and buy weakness
support: Author shows Sharpe comparison and profit factor; countertrend entries capture exhaustion events, trend followers lag entry
mechanism: Countertrend entries capitalize on institutional capitulation; trend followers buy after move already occurred
assumptions: Countertrend entries have lower win rate but better R:R

title: Pullback depth after trend break predicts reversal strength
claim: After trend line break, pullback that retraces less than 50% of the 5-bar range predicts strong reversal (3+ target); pullback that retraces >75% suggests weak reversal
support: Examples show shallow pullbacks followed by 300+ pip moves; deep pullbacks followed by 50 pip moves or bounce reversals
mechanism: Shallow pullback suggests institutional support at higher level; deep pullback suggests uncertain supply/demand

title: Multi-timeframe alignment improves intraday entry edge
claim: Intraday short entries in daily downtrend have 5-10% higher win rate and 10-20% larger avg profit than intraday shorts in daily uptrend or range
support: Author documents daily trend context filter; trading with trend has better fills and follow-through than against trend
mechanism: Daily trend represents longer institutional positioning; intraday pullbacks aligned with daily direction get better continuation
assumptions: Intraday timeframe is 10-20x smaller than daily

title: Opening range breakout predicts day direction
claim: If first 30-60 min forms opening range (high and low), breakout of either boundary in first 2 hours predicts 55-60% continuation through close
support: Author provides examples: tight opening range followed by breakout predicts day direction 55-60% of time
mechanism: Opening range aggregates overnight positioning; breakout indicates institutional direction consensus

title: Overnight gap risk impacts stop placement and edge
claim: Overnight gaps (premarket move > 1-2% from prior close) affect stop placement for overnight holds; gaps that hit stops reduce backtest profitability by 20-40% if not accounted for
support: Author warns traders to account for gap risk; shows examples of stops hit by overnight gaps eliminating profitable setups
mechanism: Premarket volume and overnight news create gaps; stops placed below prior support often hit on gap open
